basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 39.' and it opens 'Vers. 39. In pinguedine terrae et in rore coeli. Licet omnis benedictio ad Jacob venerit,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 39. In pinguedine terrae et in rore coeli. Licet omnis benedictio ad Jacob venerit, non tamen vacuus dimittitur Esau. Benedicitur enim in pinguedine | terrae, hoc est in rerum omnium copia; et in rore coeli desuper, hoc est in scientia Scripturarum, quia hoc adhuc ille populus, licet sine causa, compluitur.
